RIctzAQOe44.title: The Real Story Behind Wayland and X - Daniel Stone (linux.conf.au 2013)
RIctzAQOe44.summary: Daniel Stone, a longtime X and Wayland developer, explains at linux.conf.au 2013 why X11's design became untenable and what motivated Wayland. The talk walks through X's history and accumulated cruft.
RIctzAQOe44.why: HN treats it as the definitive, funny and educational answer to why X could not be fixed, and links it in almost every Wayland vs X argument.

quote.text: incredibly funny and educational talk[1] from 2013

YnWhqhNdYyk.title: CppCon 2015: Kate Gregory “Stop Teaching C"
YnWhqhNdYyk.summary: Kate Gregory argues at CppCon 2015 that C++ should be taught without starting from C: no char* strings, printf or raw arrays at first, with references before pointers.
YnWhqhNdYyk.why: HN people cite it constantly in C versus C++ debates as the case for teaching modern C++ idioms rather than C first.

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: Not only is she a great presenter, but she makes amazing points about what is fundamentally wrong with how C++ is taught in classrooms around the globe.

rOzrJjdZDRQ.title: [HOPE X] Elevator Hacking: From the Pit to the Penthouse
rOzrJjdZDRQ.summary: A HOPE X talk giving an in-depth explanation of how elevators work, from their history in hacker culture to using their control systems to bypass building security. It covers features and abilities of elevators that most people never see.
rOzrJjdZDRQ.why: HN commenters call it one of the most entertaining and informative con talks, and a good window into elevators from a hacker's view.

quote.text: This version is the best, with all details, no secrets withheld.

C25qzDhGLx8.title: Don't Be the Last Person to Die
C25qzDhGLx8.summary: CGP Grey argues that aging and death are a problem worth defeating, using a short animated essay. It is part of a pair with a follow-up from Kurzgesagt.
C25qzDhGLx8.why: HN longevity fans point to it as a concise, fun statement of the case for fighting aging, and some say it changed their minds.

quote.text: CGP gray's videos on YouTube are maybe the most concise and fun to watch materials I've seen on the subject.

OqjcrfKjobY.title: Tabs Outliner Overview
OqjcrfKjobY.summary: A short overview of Tabs Outliner, a Chrome extension that shows browser tabs and windows as a nestable tree. It demonstrates organizing, saving and restoring tabs.
OqjcrfKjobY.why: Commenters who struggle with tab overload use it to show what tree-based tab management looks like and recommend the extension.

quote.text: Tabs Outliner puts every tab as a leaf in a tree, and you can nest leaves

eW-OMR-iWOE.title: Honest Government Ad | Anti Encryption Law
eW-OMR-iWOE.summary: A satirical 'honest' government ad from The Juice Media about Australia's 2018 Assistance and Access anti-encryption bill. It lays out in blunt terms what the law would let authorities do.
eW-OMR-iWOE.why: Commenters recommend it as an entertaining, accessible explanation of how bad the law is, including for non-technical audiences.

quote.text: It's very entertaining, and explains it in a way that everyday people can understand how bad it will be.

0-wB1VY3Nrc.title: Humans can't read URLs. How can we fix it? - HTTP 203
0-wB1VY3Nrc.summary: Jake Archibald argues that URLs are nearly impossible for humans to interpret, especially for security. He walks through what browsers do about it, including highlighting the registrable domain, and floats a possible better design.
0-wB1VY3Nrc.why: Referenced in debates over Chrome hiding URLs as a compelling case for why full URLs are hard even for experts.

quote.text: I think they make a compelling argument for hiding most of the url in part to prevent phishing

_fZOl7C_vDI.title: David Foster Wallace reads "Consider the Lobster" (on the 2003 Maine Lobster Festival)
_fZOl7C_vDI.summary: A reading of David Foster Wallace's essay Consider the Lobster, about the 2003 Maine Lobster Festival and the ethics of boiling lobsters alive. The reading runs about 50 minutes.
_fZOl7C_vDI.why: Linked in threads about lobster welfare as an easy way to take in Wallace's essay.

quote.text: here's a video of DFW reading it out

8Q5Nur642BU.title: A Trip Down Market Street, 1906 - With Sound!
8Q5Nur642BU.summary: A sound-designed restoration of the Miles brothers' 1906 film shot from a cable car down Market Street in San Francisco, four days before the earthquake. It shows streetcars, horse carts, cars and pedestrians mixing freely.
8Q5Nur642BU.why: Cited in street-safety and self-driving threads as a picture of chaotic, shared streets before cars dominated.

quote.text: It's interesting to watch this video of San Francisco's Market street from 1906

BJEHsvW2J6M.title: 15 Mistakes Most Beginner Sourdough Bakers Make
BJEHsvW2J6M.summary: LifebyMikeG lists 15 common mistakes beginner sourdough bakers make, with advice on fixing sticky, wet dough and other issues.
BJEHsvW2J6M.why: HN bakers point to it as a good video for learning the sourdough process.

quote.text: This is a good video for learning the process

vzZy1Aqleno.title: How to Make/Build a Lifter or Ionocraft
vzZy1Aqleno.summary: A step-by-step guide to building a lifter, a small triangular ionocraft made from balsa wood, aluminum foil and thin wire, powered by a high-voltage supply. It also shows high-voltage safety practices.
vzZy1Aqleno.why: HN recommends it as a clear explanation of how lifters and ion wind propulsion work, mostly in threads about exotic propulsion and flying saucers.

6COvD8oynmI.title: Adventure with Types in Haskell - Simon Peyton Jones (Lecture 1)
6COvD8oynmI.summary: Simon Peyton Jones's first lecture on types in Haskell from the Oregon Programming Languages Summer School 2013. It covers type classes and how they relate to OOP, subtyping and polymorphism.
6COvD8oynmI.why: Mostly cited by timestamp for specific explanations, such as how type classes map to OOP and why QuickCheck is a great type class example.

quote.text: it's the coolest example of type classes Simon Peyton Jones knows and he explains why here (around 34-35 min)

IW7Rqwwth84.title: Bill Gates, Windows 98, Blue Screen of Death
IW7Rqwwth84.summary: A very short clip of Bill Gates hitting a Blue Screen of Death while demonstrating plug and play on Windows 98 on stage.
IW7Rqwwth84.why: HN cites it as the classic demo failure, in threads about USB, plug and play, and Microsoft's shipping quality.

quote.text: the infamous BSOD demo with Bill Gates on stage was meant to show off plug and play on Windows 98

IrHRQSm6LIs.title: Lies on the London Underground
IrHRQSm6LIs.summary: Tom Scott and Matt Parker investigate some of the small deceptions and oddities of the London Underground, such as misleading signage and map distortions.
IrHRQSm6LIs.why: Cited as an example of quirks caused by non-geographic maps and design choices in transit systems.

jf9I04Oa-hU.title: Nathan For You - Fixing Computer Repair
jf9I04Oa-hU.summary: A Nathan For You sketch in which Nathan Fielder tackles customers' privacy fears at computer repair shops with an awkwardly absurd business solution. It is a comedy clip from the Comedy Central show.
jf9I04Oa-hU.why: HN uses it only as a joke when computer repair privacy comes up.

rmsIZUuBoQs.title: Alan Kay on Linux
rmsIZUuBoQs.summary: A one-minute clip of Alan Kay giving his blunt critique of Linux and the Unix approach.
rmsIZUuBoQs.why: HN uses it as a quick citation of Alan Kay's dislike of Linux, in threads questioning whether the Unix way is the final word.

quote.text: the fundamental reason for why I avoid it, is best explained in this video.

tMZ2j9yK_NY.title: Willy Wonka - Funniest Clip: Machine
tMZ2j9yK_NY.summary: A one-minute clip from the 1971 film Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory in which a computer refuses to reveal its results. It plays on machines giving unhelpful answers.
tMZ2j9yK_NY.why: Used purely as a joke reference when threads feature computers or AI giving unhelpful or evasive answers.
